Yup. Did wrap the plot in print(). 

Though, the real issue, as turned out, was the server didn't support alpha transparency. Dropped alpha and specified color shades explicitly - problem solved. 

geom_bar(data =changes[changes$type2 == 'variable name',], aes(x=date, y=value, fill= variable), position = 'stack', stat='identity',alpha=1/1.5)

Appreciated you help, Stéphane. 
Cheers.

messages.subject: Re: hex color defined scale_fill_manual() works fine locally but shows no colors (blank plot) on server
parts:
I think the lack of alpha support has something to do with the devices supported on your system. If I remember correctly, if your server was compiled with cairo support, it will have transparency support, and it should default to using that when it generates PNG files. If it doesn't have cairo support, then it will use xlib, which doesn't support transparency.

One workaround is to install the Cairo package on your system or user account. (Note that this is different from having R compiled with cairo support -- the Cairo package provides the Cairo::CairoPNG() function which can be used instead of png() when creating png files.) When the Cairo package is installed, Shiny will detect it and use
CairoPNG, which has transparency support.

-Winston
